Flexible couple seeking a cheap short break

population.allocation: At least one per positive stratum, then largest remainder; individual estimate weight = target segment share / stratum sample count.

sources.title: Cathay Pacific Annual Report 2025 — HK Express operations
sources.supports: Low-cost leisure positioning, Asian destinations and aggregate passenger statistics; not the assumed target-segment weights.

sources.title: Cathay Group December 2025 traffic figures
sources.supports: Aggregate HK Express passenger counts and load factors; no matching membership conversion or segment-share table.

limitations: The reviewed official reports do not publish these customer distributions; all numerical segment weights and budget distributions remain test assumptions.
This is a deliberately targeted audience for flexible bargain travel, not a representative sample of all HK Express passengers. Fixed-date mandatory, urgent and business travel are excluded.
All sampled travellers are already valid members; no membership purchase, renewal, taxes, fuel fees or airline costs enter this experiment.
Each sampled member decides about one personal ticket; companions' purchases are outside this experiment.
Optional-trip interest, recent travel, destination appeal and the appeal of skipping are pre-price private scenario traits, not observed preferences or numerical willingness-to-pay labels.
Poststratified rates and expected revenue are estimates. Accepted ticket counts and cash revenue remain integer transactions in the cleared panel.
An LLM persona is not an independent observed HK Express customer; repeated choices do not create additional people.

rounds.accounting: Base ticket receipts only; no membership fee, tax, fuel surcharge or operating costs.

person.eligibility_reason: This optional leisure departure fits the flexible travel window.
person.travel_party_context: Any companions can use this departure and independently arrange and fund their own tickets; this decision covers one existing member only.
person.booking_trigger: Friends have agreed to be flexible about dates and destination if a cheap escape appears; nobody is obliged to make the trip.
person.departure_time_tolerance: Can adapt to the displayed departure time for a worthwhile deal; no fixed appointment requires this flight.
person.value_context: The group enjoys bargain-led trips and can use this departure. This member chooses and pays only for their own ticket; a weak deal can still be declined.
person.outside_option: Suggest another leisure outing or save for a later trip; do not invent a quoted alternative fare.
person.motivation_context: Keen to arrange an optional break, with no ticket booked and no compulsory date or destination. Has not taken a leisure trip in the last six months. This destination is acceptable but has little particular attraction today. Skipping remains possible, though arranging a worthwhile leisure break is preferred.

analysis.summary: Of 15 members, 3 bought the 552 HKD member fare and 12 declined. Nine declines were environment-forced (no ticket both available and within budget), not price objections; three cited low trip interest and optional-trip appeal, and one cited a low-interest optional trip. No customer objected to the fare itself as too high. The current fare is already at the permitted cap, so a higher test is not allowed. Evidence is mixed and thin for any directional move.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing the same 552 HKD fare on fresh members will yield a similar conversion near 17%, with declines driven mainly by availability and low trip interest rather than fare level; a materially different conversion would contradict this.

analysis.summary: At the current 326 HKD member fare, 9 of 15 customers bought and 6 declined. Four declines were environment-forced (no available ticket within budget), not price objections. The remaining two declines cited low destination appeal or low trip interest, not fare. Buyers repeatedly described 326 as a bargain versus the 690 normal fare and within their budgets. No customer objected to the fare itself. Evidence points to testing a higher fare, though buying at 326 does not prove willingness to pay more.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will retain enough purchases to raise basic ticket receipts versus 326 HKD, since no cited decline was a price objection and buyers cited large budget headroom.

initial_result.accounting: Base ticket receipts only; no membership fee, tax, fuel surcharge or operating costs.

analysis.summary: Of 16 members, 5 bought at the 470 HKD fare and 11 declined. Eight declines were environment-forced (no ticket both available and within budget), not price objections. Three declines cited low trip interest or destination appeal, and one cited a recent trip. Buyers stressed the fare as a bargain versus the 690 normal fare. No customer explicitly rejected the 470 fare as too expensive. Evidence is mixed: strong value-driven purchases but many budget-constrained declines.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a lower member fare on fresh members will raise weighted conversion enough that basic ticket receipts match or exceed those at 470 HKD, since several declines were budget-constrained rather than uninterested.

analysis.summary: At the 356 HKD member fare, five members bought and eleven declined. Most declines (eight) were environment-forced: no offered ticket was both available and within budget, which is an inventory/budget constraint rather than a price objection. Three declines cited low trip interest and a strong outside option, not fare. Buyers repeatedly described the fare as a bargain below their budgets. No customer objected to the fare itself. Evidence points to testing a higher fare, though buying at 356 does not prove willingness to pay more.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will not reduce weighted conversion enough to offset the higher per-ticket receipt, because no supplied decline cited fare as the main reason and buyers called 356 a bargain.

analysis.summary: At the current 378 HKD member fare, 3 of 16 members bought, generating 1134 HKD in basic receipts. Most declines cite low trip interest, recent travel, or keeping options open rather than the fare itself; several cite no available ticket within budget. Only one decline (DEAL-6171-00003) is primarily price-related. Buyers describe the fare as a compelling bargain well below their budgets. Evidence is mixed and thin, so a directional price test is not clearly supported.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a lower member fare on fresh members will not meaningfully raise conversion, because most declines stem from low trip interest and unavailable inventory rather than price; conversion would remain near current levels.

analysis.summary: At the current HKD 291 member fare, 10 of 16 customers bought, citing the fare as a compelling bargain; 6 declined, mostly for low trip interest or optional-trip appeal rather than price. Two declines were inventory/budget forced. No customer objected to the fare itself as too high. The fare sits well below the HKD 552 cap, and buyers repeatedly said they would decline at the HKD 690 normal fare, indicating the low fare drives conversion. Evidence supports testing a higher fare on fresh customers to see if receipts rise without losing too many buyers.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will raise basic ticket receipts per customer versus HKD 291, provided enough buyers remain; if conversion falls sharply enough that receipts drop, the higher-fare direction is contradicted.

analysis.summary: At the current 328 HKD member fare, 7 of 16 customers bought, all citing the fare as a compelling bargain against the 690 HKD normal fare. Five declines were environment-forced (no available ticket within budget), and four were low-interest or optional-trip objections despite finding the fare affordable. No customer objected to price itself. The evidence points to strong value appeal at the current fare, with remaining declines driven by availability and trip motivation rather than fare level.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will retain enough purchases to raise basic ticket receipts, since current buyers cite the fare as a bargain well below their stated budgets and no decline was price-driven.

analysis.summary: At the current 312 HKD member fare, 10 of 16 customers bought, citing the fare as a compelling bargain well below the 690 HKD normal fare and within budget. Three declines were environment-forced (no available ticket within budget), and three declined optional leisure trips for low interest or recent travel, not price. No customer objected to the 312 fare itself. Evidence supports testing a higher fare on fresh customers, though buying at 312 does not prove willingness to pay more.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will retain enough purchases to raise basic ticket receipts above the 312 HKD baseline, since no cited customer objected to price at 312.

initial_result.accounting: Base ticket receipts only; no membership fee, tax, fuel surcharge or operating costs.

decision.reason: The member fare of 552 HKD is a genuinely attractive bargain for a destination I find highly appealing, and it fits my flexible weekday window.
